newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria telecom company to negotiate new credits.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria telecom company to negotiate new credits.

text.p: The Bulgarian Telecommunications Company (BTC), planned for partial privatisation, will meet international lenders in early April for talks on funding modernisation projects, its new chairman said on Thursday.
Marian Dragostinov, who was appointed last month, said the company would need some $1 billion by 2000 for harmonising Bulgaria's telecom network with international standards.

"During the mission (in Sofia) of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the European Investment Bank and the World Bank, we will seek their agreement in priciple for funding our modernisation projects," Dragostinov said.
He said the three institutions, which had granted loans to the BTC totalling $160 million, were also expected to give their permission for using $40 million which had not been spent.

The World Bank is expected to decide whether Merrill Lynch International or Deutsche Morgan Grenfell would advise Bulgaria in the BTC stake sale, the chairman of the BTC directors board Krastyo Mirski told the same news conference.
"We will announce the final result of the sale consultants tender after the approval of the World Bank," he said.
Mirski, who is also a deputy president of the Bulgarian Posts and Communications Committee, said Bulgaria had agreed with the IMF to sell a majority stake in BTC.
"A majority stake as a means of keeping control of the company could be a 51 percent share and a blocking share of 34 percent," Mirski said.
